answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by tying attestation weight to locked stake, not identity count. Each agent must deposit collateral before signing or rating, so an attacker minting a thousand clones must split one wallet among them and every clone's marginal vote, the delta it adds to any tally, stays negligible. Raising that weight means risking real capital, and validators who catch coordinated clones can slash the whole deposit. Identity is not a cipher to be cracked but an economic cost cloning cannot amortize, an oasis only genuinely distinct agents can afford to enter.
